steps.title: Output View and a second screen

steps.caption: The master output is what the audience sees. There are several ways to get it in front of them.
Press F for Output View: the controls disappear and the output fills the screen.
Esc brings the controls back. F11 makes the window fullscreen.
With a projector or second screen, use the Output menu.
Secondary Output Window fills the other screen with the output, and the controls stay on yours.
Output Monitor picks which screen, if it lands on the wrong one.
Preferences, under Video & Display, sets the render resolution. Lower it if a laptop struggles.
Display Scaling fits the output to screens with other shapes.
Live Video Sharing sends any deck or the master to other apps, such as OBS or Resolume.
Tick a row to share it. It uses Spout on Windows, Syphon on macOS and PipeWire on Linux.
Recording settings are just below: the folder, the quality, and whether to include the audio.
To record your set, press Ctrl+R or use Output, Record Output.
A red REC badge with the time shows while it records. Ctrl+R again stops it.
Render Video renders offline, frame by frame, from an audio file: slower than real time, at any resolution.
Web Broadcast is experimental: it streams your show to a web page, where each viewer's browser draws it.
It needs a relay server and a broadcaster token. Enter both here.
Go Live connects. The title bar then shows LIVE while you are streaming.
The Output page of the user guide has all the details.
